hints: Focus on what type of compound strontium nitrate is and how Group 2 nitrates behave when heated strongly.
Remember that all Group 2 nitrates decompose to give the metal oxide plus two gases, nitrogen dioxide and oxygen.
Link each gas and the solid residue to its classic test or appearance, brown colour, relighting a splint, and colour of strontium oxide.
walkthrough:
**Recall Group 2 nitrate decomposition**

All Group 2 nitrates decompose on strong heating to form the metal oxide, nitrogen dioxide and oxygen. Strontium is no exception.

Chemical equation:
$$2\text{Sr}(\text{NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{SrO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$$

**Check statement 1 for brown gas**

Nitrogen dioxide, $\text{NO}_2$, is a distinctive brown, pungent gas. Its formation explains statement 1, so statement 1 is correct.

**Check statement 2 for relighting splint**

Oxygen, $\text{O}_2$, is the other gas product. It relights a glowing splint, so statement 2 is also correct.

**Check statement 3 for white residue**

The solid left is strontium oxide, $\text{SrO}$. Like most Group 2 oxides, it is a white powder, so statement 3 is correct.

Conclusion:
$$\text{Statements 1, 2 and 3 are all correct}$$

options.A: Correct, because all three statements are true. Brown $\text{NO}_2$ is evolved, $\text{O}_2$ relights a glowing splint, and white $\text{SrO}$ remains.
options.B: Incorrect, because it omits one true statement. Many students correctly spot the two gases but forget that the Group 2 oxide residue is a white solid.
options.C: Incorrect, because it omits the brown gas. Some students confuse nitrate decomposition with carbonate decomposition, which gives colourless $\text{CO}_2$ only, and so miss $\text{NO}_2$.
options.D: Incorrect, because it includes only one true statement. This comes from incomplete recall of the products, for example remembering $\text{NO}_2$ but forgetting $\text{O}_2$ and $\text{SrO}$.
